messages:
Nina Patel: Quick sync — I'm proposing we compress trace/telemetry headers at the edge to shrink envelope sizes and cut egress costs. Thoughts?
Samir Kaur: yes please. mobile SDKs are spamming large envelopes right now.
Alex Gomez: clarify: are we compressing the whole envelope or just the header map?
Nina Patel: plan is to keep full body unchanged for now. compress the top-level header map (trace_id, span_id, baggage, sampling tags, billing keys) into one small blob + version header. fallback to current behavior if consumer doesn't understand it.
Liz Chen: concern: some L7 filters (envoy, ext_auth) need plaintext sampling/billing keys to make routing decisions.
Maria Ortiz: and cost attribution needs canonical billing key to be visible at ingest. if we hide it, attribution breaks.
Samir Kaur: ingestion can decompress and re-expose billing_key for downstream pipelines, but that adds CPU at ingest. tradeoff to measure.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary edge-agent v0.3 rolled out to 3 regions (info).
Rajiv Singh: rough numbers: mobile daily payload ~150KB/user, headers ~30% of that. compressing headers gets ~70% header reduction => ~20% egress reduction overall. ingest CPU appears cheaper than cross-region egress at our scale.
Alex Gomez: compatibility idea: add version header `X-RW-Trace-V: c1` and `X-RW-Trace-B64: <base64>` blob. unknown headers are ignored by proxies, so graceful. Example:
```
X-RW-Trace-V: c1
X-RW-Trace-Idx: trace_id,billing_key
X-RW-Trace-B64: H4sIAAAAA...==
```
Liz Chen: also for live tailing / debugging we sometimes need to peek a couple fields without decompressing. full decompress on every router would be expensive.
Nina Patel: suggestion: include a tiny index header `X-RW-Trace-Idx` listing a few plaintext keys (comma-separated) that we guarantee remain visible. routers can inspect those cheaply, and only decompress when more fields needed.
Maria Ortiz: SDK rollout plan: default off, opt-in in mobile SDKs until we validate. docs + ingestion contracts must be clear about which keys remain visible.
Rajiv Singh: action items: Samir — perf test for ingest CPU delta; Alex — prototype header format + envoy filter to peek `X-RW-Trace-Idx`; Nina — write short RFC with fallback semantics. target: numbers + prototype by EOD Fri.
Samir Kaur: sg, I'll run tests on sample traffic and post results.
Alex Gomez: I'll push a tiny PoC branch for the envoy filter and link it here when ready.
Nina Patel: fallback plan: if we see latency regressions, fall back to agent-side gzip of the envelope for opt-in customers. :+1:
Liz Chen: :thumbsup:
Maria Ortiz: Adding a checklist for the RFC — compatibility, ingest CPU estimate, sample codecs (gzip vs snappy), SDK opt-in flags, docs.
Nina Patel: thanks all — will start the RFC draft and add the checklist.
